value.name: Daniel denies knowledge
value.description: Daniel tells Asha he does not know what she is talking about.
evidence: "I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

value.name: Asha confronts Daniel about missing folders
value.description: Asha states that Rosa said Daniel's mother kept important papers in green folders and points out that none are in the desk or room.
evidence: "Rosa says your mother kept her important papers in green folders. There are no green folders in this desk. There are no green folders in this room."

value.name: Daniel suggests his mother moved the papers
value.description: Daniel speculates that his mother may have moved the folders herself.

value.name: Asha presses Daniel for the papers' location
value.description: Asha challenges Daniel to explain where the missing papers could have been moved.
evidence: "When were you last in this room, Mr. Serrano?"

value.name: Daniel admits being in the room after the funeral
value.description: After a measured pause, Daniel says he was last in the room on the day of the funeral before the family returned to the house.
evidence: "The day of the funeral. Before everyone came back to the house. I came up to — I don't know. To stand somewhere alone."

value.name: Daniel denies opening the desk
value.description: Daniel says he did not open the desk when he was alone in the room.

value.name: Daniel denies opening any drawers
value.description: Daniel further denies opening any of the desk drawers.
evidence: "Did you open any of these drawers."

value.name: Lucia reacts silently
value.description: Lucia makes a suppressed sound behind Daniel, suggesting amusement or disbelief, and Daniel briefly turns toward her before facing Asha again.
evidence: "Lucia made a small sound behind him. Not a word. Something between a breath and the beginning of a laugh that had been amputated before it could become one. Daniel turned his head a quarter inch toward her, did not complete the turn, and faced Asha again."

value.name: Daniel insists he stayed only briefly
value.description: Daniel reiterates that he came upstairs to be alone, sat on a stool for ten minutes, and then returned downstairs without touching his mother's papers.
evidence: "I came up here to be alone," he said. "I sat on that stool for ten minutes. I went back downstairs. I did not touch my mother's papers."

value.name: Asha dismisses Daniel's statement
value.description: Asha responds with a flat, weightless thank-you that signals skepticism rather than gratitude.
evidence: "Thank you," Asha said. She let the thank-you carry no weight at all.
